Mary Baker Eddy. Eighteen twenty-one to nineteen ten. The founding figure of Christian Science, a uniquely American religion blending Christian theology with metaphysical philosophy and emphasizing spiritual healing. Born in New England, she developed a distinctive interpretation of Jesus's teachings centered on the power of consciousness and the illusory nature of material evil. Mary Baker Eddy was born in rural New Hampshire and experienced chronic illness throughout her childhood, which profoundly shaped her spiritual quest for healing and truth. She claimed to experience a sudden healing in eighteen sixty-six after a severe fall, attributing her recovery to spiritual insight and divine understanding rather than medical treatment. Her foundational text, Science and Health with Key to the Scriptures, published in eighteen seventy-five, combines biblical interpretation with metaphysical philosophy and established the theological framework of Christian Science. Christian Science teaches that God is Mind, not anthropomorphic, that matter is illusory, and that sin, sickness, and death are the result of false consciousness rather than material reality. She taught that Jesus Christ was the supreme exemplar of understanding God's true nature and that his healings demonstrated the spiritual power available to all believers through proper understanding. Eddy founded the Church of Christ, Scientist in eighteen seventy-nine, establishing a unique congregational structure with reading rooms and practicing Christian Science practitioners who provide spiritual healing. She emphasized the role of divine Science, a systematic understanding of God's laws, as superior to medical science, making Christian Science distinctive in its skepticism toward conventional medicine. Though controversial, her movement attracted thousands of followers and established institutions, publications, and a worldwide presence that continues to influence American spirituality.
